title: Reconstitution of circadian oscillation of cyanobacterial KaiC phosphorylation in vitro
author: Nakajima et al.
methods: Purified cyanobacterial clock proteins; biochemical reconstitution
finding: KaiA, KaiB, KaiC and ATP supported self-sustaining phosphorylation oscillation. Temperature compensation and agreement between mutant periods in vitro and in vivo strengthened the biological interpretation.
relevance: direct evidence for a molecular timing mechanism; a broad Alpha reference independent of OXTR.
limit: biochemical reconstruction is more informative about mechanism than visual analogy. It is a cyanobacterial system, not a mammalian receptor study, and does not support a universal exact 24-hour period or M9 correspondence.
access: primary abstract and publication metadata. Replication and detailed methods require full-text appraisal before a formal quality rating.
scoreReason: Molecular reconstitution tests a timing mechanism; appraisal currently covers the abstract and metadata.
crossrefTitle: Reconstitution of Circadian Oscillation of Cyanobacterial KaiC Phosphorylation in Vitro

title: Phase locking and multiple oscillating attractors for the coupled mammalian clock and cell cycle
author: Feillet et al.
methods: Mouse fibroblasts; live-cell imaging and modelling
finding: live imaging of proliferating mouse fibroblasts, combined with modelling, identified phase locking and additional clock states under different conditions.
relevance: direct support for studying relationships between biological cycles; connects the Alpha and Beta research themes without making them equivalent.
limit: single-cell observations support the dynamical interpretation. Culture conditions and synchronisation matter, and related cells are not automatically independent replicates. No modular doubling or Atlas geometry was tested.
access: primary abstract and selected results, including period distributions. A phase-space representation is not evidence of a physical toroidal cell structure.
scoreReason: Live-cell observations and modelling provide complementary evidence for phase locking; selected results appraised.
crossrefTitle: Phase locking and multiple oscillating attractors for the coupled mammalian clock and cell cycle

title: Interaction between time-of-day and oxytocin efficacy in mice and humans with and without gestational diabetes
author: Duong et al.
methods: Mouse genetics; human cells; retrospective human records
finding: mouse experiments support BMAL1 regulation of Oxtr and time-dependent oxytocin responsiveness. Human myometrial-cell experiments and records from 2,367 patients add distinct translational observations.
relevance: a direct OXTR connection to the Alpha theme.
limit: genetic perturbation and promoter experiments strengthen mechanism. Animal, cell and retrospective components need separate appraisal; the human observations can be confounded. Uterine findings do not establish effects in brain tissue.
access: final publication abstract and selected full-text results. The 2024 preprint is superseded for this register and is not counted as another study.
scoreReason: Genetic and promoter experiments support mechanism; the human observational component has separate confounding limits.
crossrefTitle: Interaction between time-of-day and oxytocin efficacy in mice and humans with and without gestational diabetes

title: Cryptochromes mediate rhythmic repression of the glucocorticoid receptor
author: Lamia et al.
methods: Mouse cells and mice; genetic and biochemical experiments
finding: Cry1/Cry2 interacted with the glucocorticoid receptor and altered glucocorticoid-responsive transcription in mouse cells, with related metabolic phenotypes in mice.
relevance: direct circadian–receptor evidence provides a natural NR3C1 example beyond oxytocin.
limit: molecular interactions, genetic perturbations and physiological observations complement one another. Multiple pathways change in knockout animals; the results do not isolate a universal geometric explanation or establish human clinical effects.
access: primary abstract and selected experimental/results text. NR3C1 identifies the receptor target; the principal genetic perturbations here involved cryptochromes.
scoreReason: Genetic perturbations, molecular interactions and physiological measurements support the reported mechanism.
crossrefTitle: Cryptochromes mediate rhythmic repression of the glucocorticoid receptor

title: Experimental and theoretical study of mitotic spindle orientation
author: Théry et al.
methods: Human HeLa cells; controlled adhesion geometry and modelling
finding: controlled adhesion patterns in human HeLa cells, combined with a physical model, accounted for spindle-orientation distributions across different microenvironment geometries.
relevance: direct evidence that geometry is a meaningful biological variable; supports interest in the Beta/division theme and related shape families.
limit: manipulation of the cell environment offers more than an observational resemblance. The model uses specific force assumptions and a transformed cell line. Division orientation is distinct from division rate, population doubling or a Fibonacci sequence.
access: publisher abstract and figure descriptions. Full methods and sample accounting remain to be appraised.
scoreReason: Controlled adhesion geometry tests a quantitative model; full methods and sample accounting remain open for appraisal.
crossrefTitle: Experimental and theoretical study of mitotic spindle orientation

title: Oxytocin promotes epicardial cell activation and heart regeneration after cardiac injury
author: Wasserman et al.
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
methods: Human stem-cell-derived epicardial cells and zebrafish
finding: OXT promoted activation and proliferation-related outcomes in human stem-cell-derived epicardial cells; OXTR knockdown removed the response. Zebrafish experiments supplied a separate regeneration context.
relevance: a direct OXTR-related example for the Beta research theme.
limit: receptor knockdown strengthens causal interpretation within the model. Check independent cell lines and differentiation batches; images are subsamples, not donors. Cultured epicardial cells and fish regeneration do not establish regeneration of adult human hearts.
access: primary full-text methods/results and relevant figure captions, including OXTR knockdown and proliferation measurements.
scoreReason: Receptor knockdown provides a mechanistic test alongside cell and zebrafish experiments; methods and results appraised.
crossrefTitle: Oxytocin promotes epicardial cell activation and heart regeneration after cardiac injury

title: Oxytocin stimulates hippocampal neurogenesis via oxytocin receptor expressed in CA3 pyramidal neurons
author: Lin et al.
finding: conditional Oxtr deletion in mouse hippocampal excitatory neurons affected survival and maturation of newly generated neurons, while measured progenitor proliferation and early differentiation were unchanged.
relevance: direct evidence that the biological outcome must be named precisely. It bounds generalisations from E06 without contradicting a different tissue-specific finding.
limit: conditional genetics help localise the process. Appraise cell-type specificity, blinding and precision; an unchanged measured outcome does not prove absence of every possible effect.
access: primary results/discussion. Retained deliberately to avoid presenting all OXTR growth-related findings as evidence of duplication.
scoreReason: Conditional genetics and cell-outcome measurements distinguish survival from proliferation in this mouse system.
crossrefTitle: Oxytocin stimulates hippocampal neurogenesis via oxytocin receptor expressed in CA3 pyramidal neurons

title: Structural basis for the activation and ligand recognition of the human oxytocin receptor
author: Waltenspühl et al.
methods: Engineered human receptor complex; cryo-EM and functional assays
finding: cryo-EM at 3.2 Å and functional experiments characterised OXT recognition and receptor activation. All nine peptide residues participate in binding.
relevance: a direct structural foundation for Gamma's molecular-recognition theme; useful context, but not confirmation, for the OXT-specific Epsilon proposal.
limit: structure–function comparisons strengthen interpretation. Receptor stabilisation and an engineered G protein affect generalisation. The six-residue disulfide loop is not itself an aromatic hexagon; the reported contacts do not establish an Epsilon trajectory.
access: full primary article main text, receptor-engineering description and functional-assay captions. No new molecular analysis performed.
scoreReason: Structural observations and functional residue tests provide complementary evidence; main text and assay descriptions appraised.
crossrefTitle: Structural basis for the activation and ligand recognition of the human oxytocin receptor

title: X-ray structures and mechanism of the human serotonin transporter
author: Coleman, Green & Gouaux
methods: Engineered human serotonin transporter; crystallography and assays
finding: structures of human SERT bound to antidepressants identified central and allosteric binding sites and explained aspects of inhibitor recognition.
relevance: direct structural evidence broadens Gamma beyond OXTR to SLC6A4.
limit: structural and binding/transport measurements are complementary. Thermostabilised constructs were used; the ts3 construct had no detectable transport activity. Results describe particular inhibitor-bound conformations rather than every physiological state.
access: publisher abstract and selected primary methods/results. These data concern the protein product and ligand recognition, not regulation of SLC6A4 gene expression.
scoreReason: Structures and functional measurements complement one another; engineered constructs constrain interpretation.
crossrefTitle: X-ray structures and mechanism of the human serotonin transporter

title: Structure of a D2 dopamine receptor–G-protein complex in a lipid membrane
author: Yin et al.
methods: Engineered human DRD2 complex in a lipid membrane; cryo-EM
finding: cryo-EM characterised an agonist-bound DRD2–Gi complex within a reconstituted phospholipid membrane, identifying receptor, G-protein and lipid interactions.
relevance: direct evidence for the structural context of molecular recognition; another Gamma hero example.
limit: including a lipid environment improves contextual relevance relative to isolated detergent structures. The receptor complex is engineered and ligand-bound; it does not represent every receptor state or establish clinical outcomes.
access: primary abstract and selected full-text structural results, with deposited structural metadata checked. No geometric correspondence to the Atlas was analysed.
scoreReason: A membrane-reconstituted structural observation provides a defined molecular state; independent functional validation needs fuller appraisal.
crossrefTitle: Structure of a D2 dopamine receptor–G-protein complex in a lipid membrane

title: Assembly of a π–π stack of ligands in the binding site of an acetylcholine-binding protein
author: Stornaiuolo et al.
methods: Molluscan binding protein; crystallography and solution assays
finding: an Aplysia acetylcholine-binding protein accommodated a stack of three aromatic ligands. Solution binding measurements supported the structural observation.
relevance: direct experimental support for π-stacking as a molecular-recognition phenomenon; an Epsilon reference that does not depend on OXTR.
limit: crystallography, mutagenesis and solution assays help address crystallographic-artifact concerns. This soluble molluscan protein is a model for receptor ligand-binding domains, not a complete human receptor. Neither the three-ligand count nor the stacked geometry establishes the Atlas traversal.
access: full primary main text, including solution validation and scope of the receptor model.
scoreReason: Structures, mutagenesis and solution assays support the binding interpretation; full main text appraised.
crossrefTitle: Assembly of a π–π stack of ligands in the binding site of an acetylcholine-binding protein

title: Targeted disruption of pi–pi stacking in Malaysian banana lectin reduces mitogenicity while preserving antiviral activity
author: Covés-Datson et al.
methods: Engineered plant lectin; structures and cellular assays
finding: an F84T mutation disrupted aromatic stacking in Malay BanLec, reduced mitogenic activity and retained antiviral activity in the studied assays.
relevance: a direct structure–function example for Epsilon; also connects molecular interactions with proliferation as a biological outcome.
limit: structural checks and functional comparisons strengthen the rationale. Mutation can change several properties simultaneously, so this is not a pure isolation of one energetic contribution. Plant-lectin effects do not establish OXTR behaviour or clinical benefit.
access: primary abstract and main structural/results sections. Published in 2021 despite “2020” appearing within the DOI.
scoreReason: Targeted mutation and structural / cellular comparisons connect aromatic organisation with biological outcomes.
crossrefTitle: Targeted disruption of pi–pi stacking in Malaysian banana lectin reduces mitogenicity while preserving antiviral activity

title: Reconstruction of molecular orbital densities from photoemission data
author: Puschnig et al.
methods: Organic molecular films; photoemission and calculations
finding: photoemission measurements and Fourier reconstruction yielded orbital-density distributions for pentacene films and p-sexiphenyl monolayers, compared with density-functional calculations.
relevance: direct physics evidence for studying spatial electronic structure; contextual to the valence-electron theme and more distant from biological significance.
limit: comparison of measurement and theory is valuable. Reconstruction is model-dependent and the samples are non-living materials. Orbital densities are not classical electron orbits or evidence of unicursal electron motion.
access: primary abstract and metadata. No biological role, creation-of-life claim or numeric WSS assignment follows from this paper.
scoreReason: Measurement and reconstruction are compared with calculations; current appraisal is abstract-level.
crossrefTitle: Reconstruction of Molecular Orbital Densities from Photoemission Data

title: CD38 is critical for social behaviour by regulating oxytocin secretion
author: Jin et al.
methods: Mice; Cd38 knockout and rescue experiments
finding: Cd38-knockout mice showed altered oxytocin secretion and behavioural phenotypes. Oxytocin replacement or hypothalamic delivery of human CD38 rescued selected outcomes.
relevance: direct support for CD38 involvement in the oxytocin system. Retained as supporting hero context without forcing it into a particular sequence family.
limit: knockout plus rescue strengthens causal interpretation in mice. Global deletion, behavioural measurement and human translation require careful appraisal. This concerns secretion, not proof of OXTR-expression regulation or geometric correspondence.
access: primary abstract and figure descriptions. Full methods are needed before formal risk-of-bias grading.
scoreReason: Knockout and rescue experiments test the secretion mechanism; full methods remain open for appraisal.
